correctness.rationale: For every n and real s>0, exact resource-feasibility optimization gives A=sum(phi_i/v_i), where phi_i is reconstructed from max-coalition threshold games. Summation by parts yields the rank-ratio identity. Conditional beta order statistics give the gamma-ratio expectation; Dirichlet normalized spacings and elementary finite telescoping give the exact H_n^(2), 2n/(n+1), and 3n(3n+5)/[4(n+1)(n+2)] instances. A deterministic quantile-grid Riemann argument includes explicit rank-end tail bounds. The DKW deviation bound plus summable exceptional probabilities and pair-coefficient control prove a.s. and L1 convergence. Tonelli yields the positive limiting series. Standalone verify.py produced PASS 1137 checks, including independent permutation enumeration, exact rational checks and finite simulations; no finite simulation is claimed to prove a limit.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper supplies the fixed-profile max-game Shapley formula, exact allocation feasibility and worst-case logarithmic bounds; those premises are explicitly credited. Its inspected introduction, all of Section 4, conclusion and Appendix B do not state the iid power-productivity exact expectation, second-order harmonic law, pathwise stochastic ordering or almost-sure/mean digamma limit. The 2014 max-games paper computes Shapley payoffs under fixed weights and agent-failure reliabilities but not the no-transfer fairness approximation or distributions over weights. Searches of a published mathematical-results index and web literature were conducted for max-game, Shapley fairness, uniform order statistics, harmonic-order-two and digamma aliases. No equivalent or dominating statement was identified, subject to the residual unindexed-prior-work risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed article may already compute the same expected max-game Shapley inverse-value sum or the corresponding order-statistic harmonic laws.
A general probabilistic Shapley/fairness paper not returned by the actual searches could imply the result despite different terminology.
The result assumes uncapped single-good production and does not claim priority over the fixed-profile decomposition of the primary source.

value.rationale: The exact expectation and a.s. constant quantify how much resource must be scaled to realize contribution-weighted Shapley entitlements for a natural random productivity model. The surprising H_n^(2) rather than H_n dependence separates iid typical performance from the logarithmic worst-case; the full one-parameter power family gives an exact finite-n gamma expression, pathwise stochastic order, closed limiting curve and asymptotic high-heterogeneity growth. This is a motivated and naturally dimensioned resource-allocation invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the deterministic Shapley formula. The result also gives explicit benchmarks for simulations of contribution-fair resource allocation.
